courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Poetic Roots of Hip-Hop: Hidden Histories of African American Rhyme
courses.description: What are the roots of hip-hop's masterful rhymes and tongue-tripping flow? This seminar explores hip-hop's poetic prehistory, looking to the rhyming and oral poetics that have long defined African American experience. In so doing, we'll uncover hidden histories of everyday eloquence and explore spoken/sung poetry's role in marking cultural identity. Honors version available.

source.text: FOLK 77. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-POWER.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Anthropology of the Caribbean
courses.description: Theories and examples of how Caribbean people live, act, and see themselves within various cultural, social, economic, and political contexts across time. Attention to North American views of the Caribbean.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Everyday Cultures: Folklore in America
courses.description: An introduction to the study of creativity and aesthetic expression in everyday life, considering both traditional genres and contemporary innovations in the material, verbal, and musical arts.

source.text: FOLK 202. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | ENGL 202 , ANTH 202 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Environmental Humanities
courses.description: While scientific research and technological innovation are critical to addressing the ecological challenges of our time, the environmental humanities can offer equally vital insights by examining how cultural values, artistic expressions, and ethical perspectives have formed -- and been formed by -- humans' relationships with the environment. By consulting artists, poets, writers, and thinkers, students will untangle the intertwined connection between ''nature'' and ''culture,'' tapping into key existential questions about what it means to be humans who not only live in this world, but who seek to solve the environmental problems that they have caused or exacerbated.

source.text: FOLK 205. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | ENEC 205 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: U.S. Historical Geographies
courses.description: A study of selected past geographies of the United States with emphasis on the significant geographic changes in population, cultural, and economic conditions through time. Previously offered as FOLK/GEOG 454. (GHA)

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Fairy Tales
courses.description: A study of fairy tales as historical artifacts that reveal the concerns of their times and places, as narrative structures capable of remarkable transformation, and as artistic performances drawing upon the expressive resources of multiple media, intended to challenge conventional presuppositions about the genre.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Art, Nature, and Climate Change
courses.description: This course will draw from folkloristic and anthropological theories and methods to explore how people turn to their artistic expressions--such as storytelling, painting, cooking, weaving, and more--to understand, react, and adapt to environmental changes, ranging from natural disasters to controversial land management policies. By attending to case studies of climate change at a geographically expansive scale, the course connects the local to the global and invites students to consider how environmental changes and creative expressions manifest in disparate cultural contexts. Our examination of globally diverse examples is counterbalanced by immersive experiential activities in and speakers from North Carolina.

source.text: FOLK 334. | 3 Credits. | FC-CREATE or FC-GLOBAL. | ANTH 334 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Southern Legacies: The Descendants Project
courses.description: In this Course-based Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) class, students will explore the legacy of racial terrorism in North Carolina. Students will search archival sources to discover the family histories of lynching victims, tracing those families to the present, interviewing their descendants, and working with communities to build public awareness of - and perhaps public memorials to - the victims of racial violence.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Critical Issues in Contemporary Food Studies
courses.description: Students explore, analyze, and research the politics and ethics of food debates in contemporary American culture. These include the struggles of the National School Lunch Program, the Minimum Wage Act's effect on the restaurant business, and the impact of social media on body image. Through engaging a combination of media discourse on food politics, scholarly articles, and narratives of people working in the food system, students are invited into vibrant debates. By the end of the course, students will not only analyze food systems but also design and conduct original research projects that contribute to ongoing debates in Food Studies. Restricted to Food Studies Minors and American Studies majors.

source.text: FOLK 375. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, AMST 275 or NUTR 175 . | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | AMST 375 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Ritual, Festival, and Public Culture
courses.description: This course explores rituals, festivals, and public cultural performances as forms of complex, collective, embodied creative expression. As sites of popular celebration, conflict resolution, identity definition, and social exchange, they provide rich texts for folkloristic study. We consider how local and global forces both sustain and challenge these forms.

source.text: FOLK 424. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES, RESEARCH. | ANTH 424 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Religion and Anthropology
courses.description: Religion studied anthropologically as a cultural, social, and psychological phenomenon in the works of classical and contemporary social thought. Honors version available.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Culture and Power in Southeast Asia
courses.description: The formation and transformation of values, identities, and expressive forms in Southeast Asia in response to forms of power. Emphasis on the impact of colonialism, the nation-state, and globalization.

source.text: FOLK 429. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER. | ANTH 429 , ASIA 429 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Medicine and Anthropology
courses.description: This course examines cultural understandings of health, illness, and medical systems from an anthropological perspective with a special focus on Western medicine.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Traditions in Transition: Jewish Folklore and Ethnography
courses.description: This seminar examines Jewish stories, humor, ritual, custom, belief, architecture, dress, and food as forms of creative expression that have complex relationships to Jewish experience, representation, identity, memory, and tradition. What makes these forms of folklore Jewish, how do source communities interpret them, and how do ethnographers document them? Previously offered as FOLK 380/FOLK 505/JWST 380/JWST 505.

source.text: FOLK 472. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING, RESEARCH. | JWST 472 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Anthropology of the Body and the Subject
courses.description: Anthropological and historical studies of cultural constructions of bodily experience and subjectivity are reviewed, with emphasis on the genesis of the modern individual and cultural approaches to gender and sexuality.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Graffiti, Gods, and Gardens: Urban Folklore
courses.description: What is the relationship between distinctive features of urban environments and the expressive forms found in those settings? This course explores the impact of the urban setting on folk traditions. We examine how people transform urban spaces into places of meaning through storytelling, festival, ritual, food, art, music, and dance.

source.text: FOLK 476. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Vernacular Traditions in African American Music
courses.description: Explores performance traditions in African American music, tracing development from African song through reels, blues, gospel, and contemporary vernacular expression. Focuses on continuity, creativity, and change within African American aesthetics. Previously offered as FOLK 610/AAAD 432.

source.text: FOLK 480. | 4 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | AAAD 480 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Jewish Belonging/s: The Material Culture of Jewish Experience
courses.description: What makes an object "Jewish"? This seminar examines how we think about, animate, repurpose, and display "Jewish" objects in the public realm, cultural institutions, religious spaces, and the home. We consider how makers and users negotiate objects' various meanings within the domains of prayer, performance, entertainment, and exhibition. The class curates a final group exhibition of Jewish material culture based on original fieldwork.

source.text: FOLK 481. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE, RESEARCH. | JWST 481 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Discourse and Dialogue in Ethnographic Research
courses.description: Study of cultural variation in styles of speaking applied to collection of ethnographic data. Talk as responsive social action and its role in the constitution of ethnic and gender identities.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Everyday Stories: Personal Narrative and Legend
courses.description: Oral storytelling may seem old-fashioned, but we tell true (or possibly true) stories every day. We will study personal narratives (about our own experiences) and legends (about improbable, intriguing events), exploring the techniques and structures that make them effective communication tools and the influence of different contexts and audiences.

source.text: FOLK 487. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | ENGL 487 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Topics in Folklore
courses.description: Topics vary from semester to semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Field Research
courses.description: Research at sites that vary.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Directed Readings in Folklore
courses.description: Permission of the department. Topic varies depending on the instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Myths and Epics of the Ancient Near East
courses.description: An examination of Babylonian, Canaanite, Egyptian, Hittite, and Sumerian texts from the prebiblical era, focusing on representative myths, epics, sagas, songs, proverbs, prophecies, and hymns. Honors version available.

source.text: FOLK 502. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | RELI 502 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Gender and Performance: Constituting Identity
courses.description: Examines the culturally and historically variable ways in which individuals constitute themselves as cis- or transgendered subjects or nonbinary subjects, drawing upon extant expressive resources, modifying them, and expanding options available to others. Performance of self as the product of esthetically marked or unmarked, everyday actions.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Oral History and Performance
courses.description: This course combines readings and field work in oral history with the study of performance as a means of interpreting and conveying oral history texts. Honors version available.

source.text: FOLK 562. | 3 Credits. | HI-PERFORM. | COMM 562 , HIST 562 , WGST 562 .

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Southern Music
courses.description: Explores the history of music in the American South from its roots to 20th-century musical forms, revealing how music serves as a window on the region's history and culture.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Folklore in the South
courses.description: An issue-oriented study of Southern folklore, exploring the ways that vernacular artistic expression (from barns and barbecue to gospel and well-told tales) come to define both community and region.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Introduction to Oral History
courses.description: Introduces students to the uses of interviews in historical research. Questions of ethics, interpretation, and the construction of memory will be explored, and interviewing skills will be developed through field work.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Ethnographic Method
courses.description: Intensive study and practice of the core research methods of cultural and social anthropology.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Observation and Interpretation of Religious Action
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Exercises (including field work) in learning to read the primary modes of public action in religious traditions, e.g., sermons, testimonies, rituals, and prayers.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Studies In Folklore
courses.description: Topic varies from semester to semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Honors Project in Folklore
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. For honors candidates. Ethnographic and/or library research and analysis of the gathered materials, leading to a draft of an honors thesis.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Honors Thesis in Folklore
courses.description: Writing of an honors thesis based on independent research conducted in FOLK 691H . Open only to senior honors candidates who work under the direction of a faculty member.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Public Folklore
courses.description: A graduate seminar addressing theory and praxis in public sector cultural work. Focusing on public folklore, this course explores broad issues of representation, cultural politics, and cultural tourism.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Performance Ethnography
courses.description: This seminar focuses on methods of ethnography and fieldwork ethics. Performance as theory and practice informs methodological inquiries as well as the analysis of specific ethnographic texts and case studies.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Seminar in Performance and Cultural Studies
courses.description: This course focuses on performance-related issues in the emergent field of cultural studies.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Seminar in Contemporary Performance Theory
courses.description: An advanced graduate seminar, this course will address recent developments and problems in performance theory. It will consider cross- and multidisciplinary approaches to performance as sites for consideration and debate.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Approaches to Folklore Theory
courses.description: A systematic overview of the major issues and theoretical perspectives that have informed the study of folklore historically and that are emerging in contemporary scholarship.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Art of Ethnography
courses.description: A field-based exploration of the pragmatic, ethical, and theoretical dimensions of ethnographic research, addressing issues of experience, aesthetics, authority, and worldview through the lens of cultural encounter. Field research required.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Seminar in Folklore
courses.description: Graduate seminar exploring selected topics in the theory and practice of Folklore.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Directed Readings
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Independent reading programs for graduate students.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Directed Studies
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Topics and credit hours vary according to the needs and interests of the individual student and the professor supervising the research project.

courses.subject: FOLK
courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.description: Research in a special field under the direction of staff members.
